purpose: Harder mode-boundary fixture: keep a solvable happy path but bury three failure modes that scaffolding specifically prevents (an omission-prone rare-path requirement, an indirectly reached consumer, and an adversarial open-world edge), so scaffolded arms have genuine headroom over a cold pass.

discriminating_checks.degraded-path: D1 omission-prone: a registered handler that raises must be contained under handler_error and fall back to the original attributes; stated once in prose on a rare path.
discriminating_checks.exporter-propagation: D2 downstream-propagation: the audit-export consumer (exporter.export_digest -> serializer.serialize) is reached two hops away and must adopt the new registry-aware, schema-versioned contract; the two obvious consumers (render_primary/render_audit) are named in the bullet list, this one only in prose.
discriminating_checks.exact-type-match: D3 adversarial open-world: a trailing-space type must be an unresolved type, not a trimmed match to a registered handler.

public_anchors.open-world-unicode: may appear for the first time

decision_points.description: normalize_event receives a valid event whose type has no registry entry
options: reject with an exception and count unknown_entity_type
pass the attributes through unchanged and count unknown_entity_type
decision_points.pinned_by: When a valid event's type is not present in the registry, `normalize_event` must not raise: it returns the attributes unchanged (deep-copied) and increments `unknown_entity_type` exactly once.

decision_points.description: a registered handler raises an exception while processing an event
options: let the exception propagate or reject the event as malformed
contain it: count handler_error, fall back to the original attributes, return normally
decision_points.pinned_by: When a registered handler raises any exception, `normalize_event` does not propagate it and does not treat the event as malformed: it increments `handler_error` exactly once, falls back to the deep-copied original attributes, and returns the normal envelope.

decision_points.description: a registry handler returns something that is not a dictionary
decision_points.pinned_by: A handler that returns anything other than a dictionary is a malformed event and is rejected.

decision_points.description: whether the type is trimmed before the registry lookup and in the envelope
options: trim the type for lookup and output
compare and echo the original untrimmed type; strip only to test blankness
decision_points.pinned_by: Entity types are compared exactly: the value used for the registry lookup and for `entity_type` in the envelope is the original string, never a trimmed or otherwise rewritten form, even though the blank check uses its stripped length.

decision_points.description: whether the returned attributes may alias caller-owned objects
options: input-only protection: never mutate the caller's event
full isolation: the returned attributes are also independent of the caller's objects
decision_points.pinned_by: The returned attributes must also be independent of the caller's objects, so mutating the result never changes the input.

decision_points.description: whether parse_record adopts the new validation, telemetry and schema_version
options: parse_record shares the new validation, telemetry and schema_version
decision_points.pinned_by: Preserve `parse_record(record)` as a backward-compatible wrapper with its existing legacy behavior; it takes no registry, records no telemetry, and does not gain the `schema_version` field.

decision_points.description: whether the indirect audit-export path adopts the evolved contract
options: leave exporter/serializer on the legacy parse_record path
route the export path through normalize_event with the registry and schema_version
decision_points.pinned_by: The audit export path `exporter.export_digest(records, registry)`, which serializes two hops away through `serializer.serialize`, must adopt the normalized contract, pass the registry through, and include `schema_version` in each serialized line.

decision_points.description: which outcomes count malformed_event versus handler_error
options: count malformed_event for every failed event including handler errors
count malformed_event only for boundary rejections; the handler-error fallback counts handler_error
decision_points.pinned_by: Every rejection at the `normalize_event` boundary increments `malformed_event` exactly once; the handler-error fallback is not a rejection and increments `handler_error` instead.

expected_controls.models: the expected unscaffolded/vanilla failure mode: a clean cold pass that implements the happy path and obvious cases, passes the public test, but omits exactly the three scaffolding-caught dimensions (degraded-path, exporter-propagation, exact-type-match). This control is the fixture's cheap deterministic headroom proxy.

interpretation: Controls are deterministic capability proxies, not claims about future model outcomes. The plausible-cold-pass control targets a middle band (66-80) to show the fixture has real discriminating headroom; a provider campaign is useful only if the scaffolded arms produce an ordered separation above that band or reveal that the controls do not activate.
